headline: Jimmie Johnson’s Nascar Team Valuation Reaches $450 Million
author: Randall Williams

paragraphs.text: Fri, November 20, 2026 at 10:44 AM EST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- Legacy Motor Club, the auto racing organization owned by seven-time Nascar Cup Series Champion Jimmie Johnson, has closed an $85 million investment round led by Knighthead Capital Management.
The raise values Legacy at $450 million, according to a person familiar with the matter who wasn't authorized to speak publicly about the deal.
The money will be put toward growing the team's operation and the development of a new headquarters in Moorseville, North Carolina, which is expected to open in 2028.

In July, Legacy announced a funding round with celebrity investors including Philadelphia Phillies star Bryce Harper, tennis champion Andy Roddick, Grammy-award-winner Darius Rucker and celebrity chef Guy Fieri.
Johnson said Legacy went back to raise more funds to continue to scale and grow, including adding a third race team.
With this investment, "we can truly hit our objectives to be a tier one racing operation in the Nascar series," Johnson said in an interview.
Legacy has three chartered Nascar teams that all use a Toyota Camry XSE. Drivers for this coming season will be Josh Berry, Erik Jones and Riley Herbst.
Knighthead Capital is led by its co-founder Tom Wagner, who founded the firm in 2008. Wagner owns stakes in the Las Vegas Raiders and Birmingham City Football Club.

Knighthead originally acquired minority interest in Legacy in January 2025, buying out much of the stake owned by Maury Gallagher, an airline entrepreneur. The transaction also made Johnson the majority owner of the racing organization.
"Investing and immediately deploying growth capital was part of the plan," Kyle Kneisly, a partner at Knighthead and Legacy board member, said in an interview.

The investment comes nearly a year after Nascar resolved a federal antitrust lawsuit by a settling with Michael Jordan's 23XI Racing and Front Row Motorsports. The settlement allowed Nascar teams to have permanent charters, potentially unlocking value for clubs.
